## Review Summary

**Overall verdict: APPROVED WITH WARNINGS**

The bootstrap implementation is correct for its stated scope. The MCP translation (`stdio` → `local`, merged command array, `enabled: true`) matches the consensus from the research report and the established spec in [U-03]. The `.gitignore` correctly covers all Opencode runtime directories. No credentials, no security issues, no logic changes.

Four findings require attention before or alongside subsequent tasks. None blocks merge on their own, but two (F-02, F-03) will cause confusion or workflow errors downstream if left open.

```
[F-01] Bare commit message "updates" on second commit
Category: Style
Severity: Warning
File: (git history — commit 221fe7e)
Lines: general
Description: The second commit "updates" does not follow the project convention
  (feat:/fix:/docs:/chore: prefix, imperative mood, issue reference). Based on the
  changed files (docs/planning/, .github/research/, .github/notes/), the correct
  form would be something like:
    docs(migration): add ADR 009, PRD, task breakdown, and research report (#224)
  This is an existing merge — flagging for awareness; squash or amend is not required
  post-merge unless the project enforces a clean log policy on development.
Suggestion: Enforce conventional commit prefixes via a commit-msg hook or CI lint step
  (commitlint) to prevent recurrence.
```

---

```
[F-03] tasks.md sequencing rules mislabel agent migration batch count and Task 4
Category: Documentation
Severity: Warning
File: docs/planning/copilot-to-opencode-migration/tasks.md
Lines: sequencing rule #3 (approx. lines 13–16)
Description: Sequencing rule #3 reads:
  "The agent migration is split into four batches (Tasks 5, 6, 7, 8) by family
   so each PR is reviewable. The Orchestrator family (Task 5) goes first because
   the Coder, Test Writer, Documenter, Browser, and Reflection agents are dispatched
   _by_ the orchestrator and need a working orchestrator to test through."

  Two errors:
  (a) Task 4 (Orchestrator V3 migration) is omitted from the parenthetical. There are
      five agent migration tasks (4, 5, 6, 7, 8), not four. The "(Tasks 5, 6, 7, 8)"
      list makes Task 4 look like an independent step with no sequencing constraint,
      when in fact all four listed batches depend on Task 4.
  (b) "The Orchestrator family (Task 5)" mislabels Task 5. Task 5 is
      "orchestrator's specialist sub-agents" (Coder, Test Writer, Documenter, Browser,
      Reflection). Task 4 is the Orchestrator V3 itself. A future implementer reading
      rule #3 in isolation could skip Task 4 or run it out of order.

  The causal chain is also inverted: the rule says Task 5 "goes first" because sub-agents
  need a working orchestrator, but Task 5 IS the sub-agent migration — the correct
  reason to do it first is that it validates the orchestrator from Task 4 end-to-end.

Suggestion: Replace sequencing rule #3 with:
  "3. The agent migration is split into five tasks (4–8). Task 4 (Orchestrator V3)
      must land first because Tasks 5–8 all depend on a working orchestrator to
      validate dispatch. Tasks 5–8 are batched by family (specialist sub-agents,
      reviewer, researcher, auditor+standalone) so each PR is independently reviewable."
```

```
[F-04] ADR 009 references docs/features/opencode-runtime.md without deferral note
Category: Documentation
Severity: Suggestion
File: docs/planning/adr/009-opencode-as-primary-agent-runtime.md
Lines: ~51 (Consequences → Negative section)
Description: The Consequences section states: "Documentation in
  docs/features/opencode-runtime.md must call this out explicitly." The file does
  not exist yet and is correctly deferred to Task 10 in the PRD and tasks breakdown.
  However, the ADR itself contains no "(Task 10)" qualifier, so a reader of only the
  ADR will see an unresolved requirement with no pointer to when or where it will be
  met.
Suggestion: Append "(deferred to Task 10 — see tasks.md)" to the sentence. This
  keeps the ADR self-contained and prevents future audit findings about a "missing"
  feature doc.
```

---

```
[F-05] --data-dir .chromadb is a relative path with no cwd anchor in Opencode MCP
Category: Correctness
Severity: Warning
File: opencode.json
Lines: 8
Description: The original .github/mcp.json entry had "cwd": "." to anchor the
  relative path. The Opencode MCP spec has no cwd equivalent (confirmed by GPT
  sub-agent in research report [unique finding, U-03 footnote]). Without cwd,
  `uvx chroma-mcp --data-dir .chromadb` resolves .chromadb relative to whatever
  working directory Opencode uses when it spawns the MCP process. If Opencode
  always spawns MCP processes from the directory containing opencode.json (project
  root), the path resolves correctly. If it spawns from a different directory —
  or if a developer runs `opencode` from a subdirectory — the process silently
  creates a new, empty .chromadb/ in the wrong location instead of failing.
  This has no workaround in opencode.json itself given the missing spec feature.
Suggestion: (a) Document the constraint in opencode.json as a comment or in
  docs/features/opencode-runtime.md (Task 10): "opencode must be launched from
  the project root; the chroma MCP uses a relative data-dir path."
  (b) Verify empirically during Task 2/Task 9 that Opencode does in fact anchor
  MCP process CWD to the project root; if it does not, switch to an absolute path
  using an env-var interpolation: "--data-dir", "{env:PROJECT_ROOT}/.chromadb".
```

---

```
[F-06] opencode-rules@latest is an unpinned dependency
Category: Style
Severity: Suggestion
File: opencode.json
Lines: 4
Description: "plugin": ["opencode-rules@latest"] is not pinned to a specific
  version. If opencode-rules releases a breaking change to its frontmatter schema
  or glob evaluation, rule files under .opencode/rules/ could silently stop
  matching. This is lower-risk for a bootstrap PR where no rule files exist yet,
  but will matter once Task 3 creates .opencode/rules/chromadb.md.
Suggestion: Pin to a specific semver once Task 3 validates the plugin works
  correctly (e.g. "opencode-rules@1.2.0"). Use @latest only during initial
  evaluation; pin before the full agent migration lands in Tasks 4–8.
```
